name: Grassmannian geometry and principal angles between subspaces
summary: The Grassmannian Gr(p,n) is the space of p-dimensional linear subspaces of R^n. For orthonormal basis matrices Q1 and Q2 of two such subspaces, the cosines of their principal angles are the singular values of Q1^T Q2. These angles determine several subspace distances, including the canonical geodesic distance given by their Euclidean norm (sections 2.1 and 4.3).
source_title: The Geometry of Algorithms with Orthogonality Constraints — Alan Edelman, T. A. Arias, and Steven T. Smith (1998)
caveat: Principal angles are basis-independent comparisons of linear subspaces, not pointwise polar angular gaps. The repository's sampled Givens rotations and polar-gap comparisons do not implement a principal-angle solver or establish exhaustive Grassmannian coverage or convergence.
